title: Enums and match: variants with data, Option
hints: Look at the README's 'New syntax' table: every function is one `match`, a `switch` that must cover every case and can unpack data. `is_round` is a one-liner with `matches!`.

Ideas: `area` matches on `self` (`match *self` copies the fields out) with one arm per variant; `size_word` matches `n` against ranges; `run` keeps a `Vec<i64>` as the stack, matches each op, and pops operands with `?`, so an empty stack ends the function with `None`; `greet` matches `Some(name)` against `None`.

E0004 'non-exhaustive patterns' lists exactly the cases you forgot. Mind the operand order: the first `pop()` returns the *top* value, which is `b`. E0277 'the `?` operator can only be used…' means the function doesn't return an `Option`.

Same shapes on other data: `match grade { 90..=100 => 'A', 80..=89 => 'B', _ => 'F' }` · `Msg::Move { x, y } => x * y,` · `Op::Max => { let (y, x) = (q.pop()?, q.pop()?); q.push(x.max(y)); }` · `match title { Some(t) => format!("Dr. {t}"), None => "Doctor".to_string() }`
